_meta.herkomst: De vaste teksten van het platform (PLAN #33.2, B74). Geschreven door Claude: het Engels is de bron, de andere talen volgen het. Nog niet nagelezen door een moedertaallezer; zet `nagelezen` op true als dat gebeurd is. Eigen werk, AGPL-3.0.

teksten.kernzin: Factiz collects the fact-checks of {redacties} newsrooms worldwide in one place: {paginas} claims, searchable in 15 languages, so you don't have to search every site separately.
teksten.db_kop: Is there a global fact-check database?
teksten.db_antwoord: No database holds every fact-check in the world. Factiz brings {paginas} claims that {redacties} newsrooms checked, in {talen} languages, together behind one search box, and you can read every check in 15 languages.
teksten.db_elders: Google Fact Check Explorer searches the fact-checks that newsrooms mark up for Google. The Duke Reporters' Lab keeps a list of fact-checking organisations around the world, and the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) a list of its members. Factiz adds one archive with the verdict, the newsroom and a link to its article, grouped into themes and dossiers.
teksten.db_a1: The claims are in {talen} languages. The site is in 15: English, Dutch, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Indonesian, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Hindi, Arabic and Persian. A claim keeps its own language; a translation is a machine translation and says so.
teksten.db_a2: No. Factiz holds what newsrooms publish under an open licence, and the reports of EUvsDisinfo. Many large fact-checkers do not share their checks openly yet, so not all of them are in it.
teksten.db_a3: In the archive, the newsroom that checked the claim: Factiz shows its verdict and links to its article. Factiz Radar holds Factiz's own fact-checks, checked with AI and reviewed by the editors.
teksten.db_v4: Can Factiz check any message, in any language?
teksten.db_a4: No. Factiz shows whether a claim has already been checked, and by whom. It does not check every message itself; Factiz Radar checks a few claims a week that circulate widely on X.
teksten.db_a5: Yes. Searching needs no account, and the site does not store what you type.
teksten.db_v6: Where does the data come from?
teksten.db_a6: From the fact-checks that newsrooms share through Google Data Commons under a CC BY licence, and from EUvsDisinfo. The sources page lists every source and its licence.

teksten.platform_inleiding: Factiz is building a public archive of what newsrooms have checked. This page names every part and says how far it is.
teksten.platform_producten_p1: The archive is the first product. Every claim has one page: the claim, the newsrooms that checked it, their verdict in their own words and a link to their article. Search, filters, themes and dossiers lead to it.
teksten.platform_producten_p2: Two products will follow that do not exist yet: an interface that lets a newsroom or a platform ask whether a claim was already checked, and a browser extension that shows this next to what you read.
teksten.platform_ontwikkelaars_p1: Every claim keeps its number, in every language of the site. The address of a page does not change, so you can link to it. The pages are plain HTML and work without scripts.
teksten.platform_ontwikkelaars_p2: Every edition is one file, built from sources we may republish. The sources and licences page names them. A public interface to query the archive is planned; it does not exist yet.
teksten.platform_motorkap_stap1: We take fact-checks from sources that allow it, and name the source and the licence of every record.
teksten.platform_motorkap_stap2: When several newsrooms checked the same claim, their checks share one page.
teksten.platform_motorkap_stap3: A newsroom's verdict is shown in its own words. We sort verdicts into a small set of labels. Factiz adds no verdict of its own.
teksten.platform_motorkap_stap4: A language model translates claims. We read a sample per language first, and the original always stays visible.
teksten.platform_motorkap_stap5: A language model files each claim under a theme. We read a sample of that first as well.
teksten.platform_motorkap_stap6: A language model suggests which fact-checks belong in a dossier. A second model reads every suggestion and opens the fact-check itself when the claim alone is not enough. A person decides every case in doubt and where the dossier ends, and approves it before it goes online.
teksten.platform_documentatie_p1: Where every record comes from, and under which licence, is on the sources and licences page. To cite a page, use its address: it stays the same. More documentation will follow with the interface.
teksten.over_inleiding: Factiz keeps a record of what newsrooms have checked: who checked a claim, when, and what they found. We do not decide what is true. The sources are the verdict.
teksten.over_wat_kop: What we do, and what we do not
teksten.over_wat_p1: A claim that was debunked can come back: in another language, about another object, years later. The work of the newsroom that checked it is then hard to find. Factiz puts that work side by side, so you can see that a claim was already checked, by whom and with what result.
teksten.over_wat_p2: We add no verdict of our own to a newsroom's check, and we never show a percentage of truth. If you want to know why something is false, read the newsroom's article; the link is with every check.
teksten.over_fout_p1: If a claim is filed under the wrong theme, a translation is off, or a fact-check does not belong in a dossier, write to us. Name the address of the page. We look at it; what is wrong, we correct in the next release.
teksten.over_privacy_p1: The site sets no cookies, does not track visitors, loads nothing from other parties and has no accounts. A search is not logged. We only count it anonymously, as described below.
teksten.over_privacy_tellen: Per day, we count how many pages of each kind are viewed, how many searches found nothing, and what people search for: a typed search of at most eight words, without an email address or phone number, added up anonymously. Searches that come up fewer than three times in a week are deleted. We do not keep your IP address, a cookie or which fact-check you read.

teksten.meten_vraag: May we measure how you use Factiz with Google Analytics? It sets cookies, only if you say yes.
teksten.voet_meten: Cookies and measuring only with your yes.
teksten.over_privacy_p1_meten: Without your yes, the site sets no cookies, does not follow you and loads nothing from other parties. There are no accounts. A search is not logged on our server. We only count it anonymously, as described below.
teksten.over_privacy_meten: If you say yes to the question at the bottom of the page, Google Analytics measures how you use the site: which pages you view, how you arrived (through Google or a link, for example), on what kind of device and in which country, and a short search you type. For this, Google sets cookies and the data goes to Google, including in the US. We use it to make the fact-checks easier to find. Google signals and advertising are off, we share nothing with other Google services and the data is kept for two months. A pasted message, a long search or anything with an email address or phone number never goes to Google. If you say no, the site loads nothing from Google. You can change your choice at the bottom of every page.
